why: Fields the read-back may leave unsaid. Each is either a compile-time marker the runtime never reads, or a value the surrounding words already fix — the perturbation the check makes isn't a proc the compiler could produce. Anything new fails scripts/verify/readback.mjs.

patterns.do[].sel.yours: compile-time marker for "one of your X" (compiler.js equalTo); owner:'you' carries the meaning
patterns.do[].sel.ref: steps whose wording only ever takes "that card" (put it into your hand, play it); ref:false isn't a proc they can have
patterns.do[].mods[].n: with nOf the sign is the verb (loses / gets +), which the read-back shows; the size is the stat
patterns.do[].filter.zone: a filter with any:[…] per-zone branches — the branches name the zones
patterns.effect.n: selfCost n:99 is "for free", which the read-back says
patterns.do[].sel.chosen.types[]: "cards from under chosen character, item, or location" — the source types read as "the chosen card"
patterns.effect.of: deck rule copies: the card itself
patterns.do[].n.n: 1 per counted card ("a number of cards equal to …")
patterns.do[].n.per.count.under: Bambi/Pete: "equal to the number of cards under him" — the count is shown
patterns.do[].dur: Remember Me: grantPlayFrom lasts the turn by its own wording
patterns.do[].linked: a step that follows a pay-to step is linked and ifDid at once; the if-you-did is shown
patterns.do[].do[].discard.n: "discards a non-character card of their choice" — always 1
patterns.effect.per.count.did.n.gte: "for each … banished this turn" counts them all; the threshold is unused
